chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Al-Sha'iri, from Al-Hakam ibn Uteyba, who said:

We were at the door of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and we were a group waiting for him to come out, when a woman came and said, 'Which one of you is Abu Ja'far?' The people said to her, 'What do you want from him?' She said, 'I want to ask him a question.' They said to her, 'This is the jurist of the people of Iraq, so ask him.' She said, 'My husband died and left a thousand dirhams, and there was due to me from my dower five hundred dirhams. So I took my dower and I took my inheritance. Then a man came and claimed a thousand dirhams against him, so I testified for him.'

Al-Hakam said, 'While I was calculating what she would receive, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) came out and said, 'What is this that I see you moving your fingers with, O Hakam?' So I informed him of the woman's statement and what she asked about. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'She acknowledged a third of what is in her hands, and there is no inheritance for her.'
Al-Hakam said, 'By Allah, I have not seen anyone more understanding than Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: How is a widow's inheritance calculated when a creditor claims the estate after she has already taken her dower and share?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the jurisprudential principle of *qabd* (possession) in inheritance distribution, where Imam al-Baqir (AS) rules that the widow’s prior appropriation of the estate for her dower and share effectively treats those portions as already distributed, thereby reducing the creditor's claim against the remaining balance. The Imam’s concise verdict highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the practical administration of the estate and the priority of settled claims over theoretical division, a nuance often discussed in *fiqh* commentaries regarding the timing of debt settlement relative to inheritance allocation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zakariyya Bin Yahya, from Al Shairi, from Al Hakam Bin Uteyba who said, 
‘We were at the door of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, and we were a group awaing him<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> comes out, when a woman came over. So she said, ‘Which one of you is Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>?’ So the group said to her, ‘What do you want from him<sup>asws</sup>?’ She said, ‘I want to ask him<sup>asws</sup> a question’. So they said to her, ‘This here is a jurist of the people of Al-Iraq, so ask him (instead)’. She said, ‘My husband died and left a thousand Dirhams, and there is still outstanding upon him, for me, my dower of five hundred Dirhams. So I took my dower and I took my inheritance. Then a man came over, so he claimed a thousand Dirhams against him. So I testified for him (that such is the case)’. 
So Al-Hakam said, ‘So while I was calculating what is for her, when Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> came out, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is this which I<sup>asws</sup> see you moving your fingers, O Hakam?’ So I informed him<sup>asws</sup> with the words of the woman, and what she asked about?’ So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She acceptes with a third of what is in her hands, and there is no inheritance for her’.
Al-Hakam said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I have never seen anyone of more understanding that Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zakariya ibn Yahya from al-Shu‘ayriy from al-Hakam ibn ‘Utaybah who has narrated the following:

“Once we were with abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. We were in a group waiting for him (the Imam) to come out. A woman came and asked, ’Which one of you is abu Ja‘far?’ The people asked, ‘What for are you asking for him?’ She replied, T want to ask him about an issue.’ They said, ‘This is the jurist of the people of Iraq. You can ask him your question.’ She said, ‘My husband has died and has left one thousand dirham as legacy. He owed me five hundred dirham as my mahr (dower) and my share of inheritance which I took from the legacy but then a man came and said my husband owed him one thousand dirham and I testified in his favor.’

Al-Hakam has said, ‘I was calculating it that abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, came out and said, ‘Why is it that I see you move your fingers, O Hakam?’ I replied, ‘This woman has mentioned that her husband has died. He has left one thousand dirham as legacy. He owed to her five hundred dirham as her mahr (dower). She took her dower and the share of her inheritance but then a man came and said that her husband owed him one thousand dirham and she testified in his favor.’ Hakam has said, ‘By Allah I had not completed my words that he (the Imam) said, ‘She has confessed to give back one-third of what she has in her hand and she does not have anything as her share of inheritance.’

Hakam has said, ‘I had never seen, by Allah, anyone more intelligent than abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.”’ [Note: The next several passages of the Arabic text are words of al-Fadl and are not translated.]
